key_insight: At affordable mesh resolution, brittle-fracture simulations of cooled dark chocolate cannot match elastic slope, peak force and crack path with a single parameter set, so calibration must prioritize a stated objective.
engineering_relevance: Objective-specific calibration supports simulations of food breakage during processing, transport and consumption.
method: Assess sharp-interface and diffuse phase-field models of Griffith-type brittle fracture.
Identify elastic parameters from pre-crack tension and compression, then critical energy release rate from three-point-bending peak force.
Calibrate phase-field width last, accounting for mesh-resolution constraints.
evidence_signal: The case study evaluates both frameworks on cooled dark chocolate, examining structural response, crack curvature and stress fields at an affordable spatial discretization.
watch_item: Phase-field width affects the predicted response and is constrained by mesh resolution; report the calibration objective, numerical parameters and boundary value problem together.
paper_title: Finite Element Modeling of Fracture in Brittle Foods with Physically Consistent Parameter Calibration: A Practical Case Study on Cooled Dark Chocolate
